title: Tallinn in the Hanseatic League
show: History of the Germans from the Middle Ages to Reunification
episode: Ep. 110: The Hanseatic League (1143-1669) - The Economics - Riga, Tallinn, Dorpat, Narva
description: How German merchants built a trading network around the Baltic, and how Tallinn, then called Reval, grew rich as a link to Russia. The Great Guild Hall on Pikk Street, built in the 1400s for the richest merchants, is now the history museum.

title: Peter the Great takes Tallinn
description: How Russia took Estonia from Sweden in the Great Northern War, and Tallinn surrendered in 1710. Peter the Great then built Kadriorg Palace and its park east of the old town, named for his wife, Catherine.

title: A cyberattack after a statue moved
description: Journalist Tim Weiner and former Estonian president Toomas Hendrik Ilves on the 2007 cyberattacks that shut down Estonian banks and websites, after the city moved a Soviet war memorial, the Bronze Soldier, to this military cemetery.

episode: The "Singing Revolution" and the Estonian Song and Dance Festival with Maris Hellrand
description: Journalist Maris Hellrand on the song festival, first held in 1869 and now held here every five years, with choirs of tens of thousands, and on how mass singing in 1988 became a peaceful protest against Soviet rule.

episode: Tall Stories 493: The Tallinn Song Festival Grounds

title: The night the Estonia sank
description: Investigative journalist Stephen Davis hears from survivors of the MS Estonia, the ferry that left Tallinn for Stockholm on September 27, 1994, and sank in a storm. 852 people died. The Broken Line memorial stands by the old town walls.
